originality.rationale: The exact type-B polar is the box with pairwise absolute-value edge constraints. A two-regime strictly convex bound in the maximal clique coordinate proves both the global maximum norm and all its equality cases. Polar/primal duality identifies all contact facets; antipodal pairs show origin optimal and the active-normal span proves the incenter dimension. Strict slack for finitely many remaining vertices proves existence of all small clique translations. The enclosing ball follows from the signed norm-sqrt(2) edge roots. Exact rational checks compare enumerated small polar vertices with the formulas.

value.rationale: For the natural graph-associated type-B root-polytope construction, the theorem gives a sharp structural phase boundary at a clique-to-independent-class ratio of three, exponentially different tangent-facet orbits, and a p-dimensional-to-zero-dimensional collapse of optimal centers.
